items.title: 66100_Bud Freeman oral history interview
items.q: we had a radio show, the Coca-Cola Hour... Ray was a fine musician... I was with him 18 months.

ctx.x: All right, Bud, you try this and we will get a shot on this.

I used to go see a lot of British plays when I was a kid and I got to understanding the language pretty well and liked English. So Ray would talk, you know, he was a Cambridge graduate and we had a radio show, the Coca-Cola Hour, which was quite a big thing in those days and Ray would get into the control room during rehearsals and give orders, talk out to the fellows, and he would say, 'Fellows, take the last eight bars and (unintelligible). They couldn't understand him. They'd come over and they'd say to me,…

it was Wilbur well, I didn't want to mention his name, I might say that one of the men in the band was having an affair with a married woman, and it was a habit every Tuesday morning to show up at the rehearsal at such and such a studio at CBS at 10:00. No one had to say the night before that we have a rehearsal tomorrow, you just automatically went there.
